articleTitle: High Order Polynomial Projection Operators for Circuit Macro-Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Having behavioural models for analog circuits is an important part of the design flow. With the constant evolution in the state-of-the-art of hardware technology, developing accurate circuit models is very important. Traditionally, integrated circuit macro-modeling requires strong circuit design knowledge and expertise, but this is both time-consuming and expensive. Recently, there have been works for automating the generation of behavioural models using machine learning at both the device and circuit levels. In this paper, we introduce a new type of non-linear circuit macro-model that is built on top of the high order polynomial projection operator (HIPPO) framework. We show the validity and superior performance of our HIPPO-based macro-model on a low-noise amplifier circuit example.

articleTitle: Current Density Prediction Using Neural Operators
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Simulating complex phenomena in electrical systems often involves solving partial differential equations (PDEs), which are computationally expensive and time-consuming. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly the use of neural operators, offer a promising approach to solving these problems more efficiently. This work investigates the application of neural operators to accelerate simulations in electrical engineering to predict behavior in printed circuit board transmission lines under varying frequency conditions and geometries. The study focuses on the prediction of the current density field on microstrip (slot and serpentine) transmission lines.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Prediction of Temperature-Dependent Dielectric and Conductive Parameters Based on Differential Stripline Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: The design of automotive high-speed interconnects requires the use of broadband material models that consider a wide range of environmental conditions, e.g. temperature and humidity. However, even for nominal conditions these models are nontrivial to generate. This paper extends our previous work on data-driven predictors used for the estimation of dielectric and conductive parameters of high-speed material models. Parametrized frequency-domain simulations of a differential stripline at various temperatures yield a dataset of modal propagation constants, and characteristic impedances up to 25 GHz. These inputs are used to train a 1D Convolutional Neural Network to estimate the temperature-dependent conductive and dielectric model parameters for the cannoball Huray and wideband Debye models, respectively. The trained model shows good accuracy after training/testing. Additional simulations outside the training/test dataset are used for further model validation with good agreement between predictions and expected values.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Analysis of Land-Side Capacitor Integration in LPDDR5 Dram
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper presents a thorough study on the potential benefits of Cap-on-Package (CoP) structures in handling the demands of high-performance computing. We particularly focus on the efficiency of incorporating a Land-Side Capacitor (LSC) into DRAM to enhance Power Integrity. Our findings indicate that a higher Power Distribution Network (PDN) resistance substantially reduces peak-to-peak voltage at the DIE pad by approximately 49 %, whereas a lower resistance results in minimal reduction. Additionally, multiple path segments collectively influence the power distribution network's impedance, significantly impacting Power Integrity (PI).

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependent Mutual Inductance in Broadside-Coupled Superconducting Striplines
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This study examines the mutual inductance that depends on the frequency of broadside-coupled superconducting striplines fabricated via the SFQ5ee process. Using Zimmermann's complex conductivity model put into a frequency-related surface impedance setup, mutual inductance was determined for striplines of widths <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w=0.25 \mu\ \mathrm{m}, 0.35 \mu\ \mathrm{m}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5 \mu\ \mathrm{m}$</tex> through HFSS simulations. The findings show that mutual inductance increases as the width of the stripline decreases and becomes steady at lower frequencies. At the gap frequency, the HFSS simulations were very precise, with a maximum error of only 1.1 % when compared to the experimental data, which is much better than the wxLC simulations with errors as high as 9 %. These results improve our knowledge of the mutual inductance in submicron superconducting striplines and offer a reliable method for designing and enhancing scalable superconducting integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Efficient Synthesis and Simulation of High-Density Interconnects Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This work develops a machine learning (ML) model for modeling and simulating high-density interconnects, aiming to reduce the computational time and memory requirements of electromagnetic simulations. It employs two supervised ML models: one predicts the physical parameters of interconnects from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>-parameters specifications, and the other predicts <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> parameters over a specified frequency range. Training data is generated through electromagnetic simulations with randomly varied design parameters. This randomness in the data allows for efficient training of ML models with high accuracy, even when using a small training dataset. The effectiveness of these ML models is evaluated on a stripline structure and achieves a prediction accuracy of 97 %. This approach leads to faster design processes and accurate signal integrity analysis for high-speed, high-density interconnects.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Analysis and Measurement of Thin Film Microstrip Lines (TFMSLs)
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper investigates Thin-Film Microstrip Lines (TFMSLs) for high-frequency and high-data-rate applications, including fifth-generation (5G) communication systems. Two test structures with varying spacings (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_{\text {signall }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_{\text {signal } 2}$</tex>) are analyzed in the frequency domain using mixed-mode S-parameters for both differential and common modes, validated against measurement results to confirm the accuracy of the circuit models. Time-domain analyses, based on eye diagram metrics, evaluate the signal integrity of high-speed data link systems. The study provides design maps offering specific insights into optimizing TFMSL configurations and receiver setups to ensure reliable signal transmission in high-speed digital systems.

articleTitle: Fine-Pitch Interconnect Modeling Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have been demonstrated to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) effectively and show promise in electromagnetic (EM) analysis. In this study, we compare several PINN implementations for quasi-static modeling of fine-pitch interconnects. Our results indicate that imposing hard-constrained boundary conditions and implementing a superposition-based solution significantly improves the accuracy of multi-conductor interconnect modeling.

articleTitle: Analysis of BGA/Socket Differential Signal Pin-Field Egress For Improved Signaling Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Higher I/O data rates and increasing server design feature support is resulting in high BGA and socket pin density from generation – to – generation. Increase in pin count drives tighter BGA and socket pin pitches which force a trace geometrical reduction “Neck – down” in the pin – field region to enable signal egress. The “Neck – down” coupled with a high density of signal pins results in performance degrading due to multiple reflections and crosstalk. Applying electromagnetic modeling a CuMax pin field egress is analyzed showing benefits in impedance matching minimizing exposure to multiple reflections, reduced differential to common mode conversion and far end crosstalk (FEXT) to adjacent signal with negligible layer – to – layer crosstalk when compared to the reference traditional techniques without the application of additional metal shapes.

articleTitle: Navigating the Signal Seas: Addressing MIPI C-PHY Signal Integrity Challenges in a Typical Camera Module
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: MIPI C-PHY system faces unique challenges due to its tri-level signaling, mapping, and encoding schemes along with high-speed data transmission. This paper addresses the SI/PI challenges and the mitigation techniques essential for a typical Camera modules with high-performance requirements.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low PDN Impedance Measurement Using Very Short Time Domain Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper presents three fast acquisition measurement methods suitable for high current, active, power plane impedance measurements. The 2-port shunt through impedance method, using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) has been used extensively for accurate impedance measurement of active power planes. As the core current continues to increase, the 2-port shunt through method is reaching its limits.

articleTitle: Stability of VinC LIM in Power Distribution Network Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This work examines the stability properties of the latency insertion method in the analysis of complex interconnection schemes such as power distribution networks. We specifically study the voltage-in-current formulation of the algorithm and its ability to ensure unconditional stability. A basic circuit cell is defined and analyzed to derive the conditions for stability. It is found that for the particular basic cell, the algorithm is unconditionally stable. These properties are illustrated through several network examples.

articleTitle: Dimensional Analysis and Fpga-Based Implementation for Real-Time Thickness and Conductivity Estimation in Eddy Current Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In quality control systems, the accurate and efficient measurement of material properties, such as thickness and electrical conductivity, is crucial to ensure product quality and process reliability. This paper presents a novel approach that combines the computational efficiency of Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) with the well-celebrated Buckingham's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> theorem (dimensional analysis) to address these measurement challenges. By leveraging dimensional analysis, the proposed method reduces the complexity of parameter estimation in Eddy Current Testing (ECT) by systematically eliminating redundant variables, enabling real-time processing with minimal computational overhead. The FPGA hardware implementation exploits its parallel processing capabilities to achieve high-speed data acquisition and parameter extraction, even within constrained computational resources, and seamlessly integrates into Industry 4.0 quality control systems. Experimental results demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the FPGA solution with respect to classical implementations, as well as its superior processing speed and efficiency.

articleTitle: Unified Pre-Processing Steps Reducing the PCB Design Space to Enable ML Applications for Signal and Power Integrity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) applications need large quantities of data spanning the complete Printed Circuit Board (PCB) design space. This design space needs to be reduced to the subset of relevant PCB configurations, i.e. those yielding network parameters which are different from each other. For this purpose a preliminary design space analysis is carried out and pre-processing steps are presented to unify the application of ML in the Signal and Power Integrity domains and pave the way to a standardized PCB representation format.

articleTitle: Measurement and Modeling of Bias-Dependent Powder Cores Permeability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This contribution treats the experimental and mathematical characterization of permeability spectra of magnetic powder materials subject to significant DC-current bias levels. The permeability spectra of two different commercial powder cores are experimentally measured and processed through two different modeling approaches, which allow exploiting the gathered data to properly predict the electrical behavior of high-frequency inductors built upon the considered magnetics, for the sake of system level simulation and optimization. The performance of the two approaches are compared and one example of EMI filter inductor design driven by the considered parameterized characterization is presented.

articleTitle: Worst Eye Performance Analysis for Advanced Package Die-to-Die Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper presents a time-efficient approach to identify the worst bit based on crosstalk summation calculation, and subsequently generate the corresponding worst bit patterns using PDA analysis for eye-diagram simulations. The worst bit patterns are specifically derived based on the rectangular eye mask. This method is validated and demonstrated on the UCIe application in the chip-last fanout chip on substrate (FOCoSCL) advanced package. When compared with crosstalk summation and eye-opening across various input sequences (the proposed method, PRBS7 with even- and odd-mode, PRBS18), the proposed approach shows the best correlation and the worst eye-opening result. Regarding the worst eye-opening for the worst bit, both the proposed method and the BER contour at the 1E-15 level from the VerifEye simulator show 17 % worse performance than PRBS18, while PRBS7 with even- and oddmode exhibits a 14% worse result.

articleTitle: Hybrid-Type Power-Over-Data-Line Filters for Mode Conversion Noise Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach for mode conversion noise reduction under asymmetric bias conditions in Gbps-class power-over-data-line (PoDL) communications. The proposed approach provides a hybrid circuit configuration of regular inductor components and differential mode inductors as a PoDL filter circuit configuration that is unlikely to experience imbalance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P} / \mathrm{N}$</tex> electrical characteristics caused by asymmetric bias voltages of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{P} / \mathbf{N}$</tex> components. By applying this configuration, mode conversion noise can be suppressed over a wide frequency range from 1 MHz to several GHz under asymmetric bias conditions.

articleTitle: Efficient Multiconductor Transmission Line Analysis via Hybrid Deep Equilibrium NN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient analysis method for multiconductor transmission line interconnects by developing a novel Hybrid Deep Equilibrium Neural Network architecture. In the proposed approach, smaller lumped segments are used to train a combined recurrent and convolution networks with deep equilibrium model. Validating examples demonstrate significant speed-up using the proposed method while providing responses that match reasonably well from computationally expensive higher-order models.

articleTitle: Design and Electrical Modeling of High-Speed Interfaces in a Novel Chiplet Package
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Next generation Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet-of-Things (IOT), Industrial and Automotive Networking microprocessors have high performance requirements without having to compromise on the overall system cost. These applications require large memory capacity with low latency, improved power delivery network (PDN) and high Input/Output (I/O) pin count to control the peripheral devices. Using Chiplet package technology the memory interface and passive devices needed for improved PDN can be integrated using fan-out package technology and final connection to PCB can been implemented through laminate technology. This work demonstrates the electrical analysis done to evaluate the signal integrity of high-speed digital interfaces like DDR and SerDes in a novel Chiplet package in comparison to a traditional Flip-Chip Plastic Ball Grid Array (FCPBGA) package.

articleTitle: A Hammerstein Approach for Compact Model of Nonlinear Circuits With Arbitrary Terminations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: We formulate a behavioral model order reduction approach for nonlinear circuits based on the canonical Hammerstein architecture. The work extends the ideas of [1] to arbitrary loads and improves the efficiency of the model inference by training the linear time invariant (LTI) block in the frequency domain. We demonstrate the approach with an LM741 operational amplifier and present simulation results showing its application over a range of input frequencies and loads.

articleTitle: Near Field Radiated EMI Signature Characterization of Modular Power Converters Based on Dual Active Bridge: From Calibration to Results
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental results and analysis of near-field probe measurements of a modular converter consisting of 4 dual active bridge (DAB) conversion standard cells connected in an input-parallel, output-series (IPOS) configuration. The experimental setup and the calibration process for the near-field probes are first discussed. Following this, the experimental results and a discussion on the radiated EMC signature of the modular converter are presented. The aim of this work is to explore their predictability and correlations of radiation, irrespective of the configuration used. Non-invasive measurement for co-relating with power converter parameters, e.g. ZVS performance are demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Extension of Vector Fitting to Weakly Nonlinear Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper describes a macromodeling algorithm to build behavioral models of nonlinear systems and components in a data-driven manner. The main tool is an extension of the Vector Fitting algorithm to perform rational approximation of multivariate transfer functions that describe nonlinear systems according to Volterra series theory. In addition to the rational model, a realization in terms of differential equations is provided so as to enable time-domain simulation. The raw data required by this algorithm can be extracted by means of Harmonic Balance analysis or from X-parameters, both available in commercial software.

articleTitle: High Frequency Analysis of Cu-CNT Based Tapered TSV Bumps
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In latest development of three-dimensional integrated circuit technology, tapered through silicon via (TSV) bumps are becoming a popular alternative to traditional cylindrical structure due to extremely low coupling and volume fraction, which leads to reduced crosstalk delay and better signal integrity. The tapered TSV bump structure is filled with Cu-CNT composite, which can exhibit better mechanical, thermal and electrical properties. The electrical equivalent for tapered TSV has been modeled along with redistribution layer (RDL). In this work, crosstalk and power loss analyses have been carried out. Further, we report that Cu-CNT composite TSVs outperform Cu and CNT TSVs. In addition, analysis of the different bump structures has been presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Shadow Void Optimization of Microelectronic Packages with Tree-Based Learners
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Shadow voiding is a critical technique for optimizing second-level interconnect (SLI) designs in microelectronic packages, aiming to minimize impedance mismatches while adhering to manufacturing and electrical constraints. This paper introduces a tree-based active learning algorithm for shadow void optimization. The proposed method efficiently explores geometric design parameters using decision trees and truncated SVD to reduce dimensionality. High-performing designs are identified via penalized regression within partitioned subspaces and evaluated through sequential sampling. The algorithm is applied to a 7-2-7 package, demonstrating significant improvements in electrical performance and computational efficiency. Results show that tree-based learners effectively characterize the design space, making them a practical solution for high-dimensional optimization problems in microelectronics.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap: Correlating IBIS-AMI Simulations with Post-Silicon Measurements for a 6.25 Gbps Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: From the SI(Signal Integrity) perspective, IBIS (Input/Output Buffer Information Specification) models are widely used in system design and performance analysis using channel & board packages. The accuracy of IBIS models has a significant impact on system performance and the overall design cycle. In this paper, a comprehensive comparison is presented between the simulation results obtained using IBIS-AMI (Input/Output Buffer Information Specification - Algorithmic Modeling Interface) models and post-silicon measurement results for a PHY (Physical Layer) transmitter operating at 6.25 Gbps. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the accuracy and reliability of IBIS-AMI simulations in predicting the real-world performance of high-speed serial interfaces. Extensive simulations were conducted using Signal-Integrity toolbox of MathWorks®, and various electrical parameters were extracted in alignment with IP-specified methodologies. The results demonstrate a high degree of correlation between the simulated and measured data, validating the efficacy of IBIS-AMI models in design of complete system involving high speed PHY operating in real world with lossy channel.

articleTitle: Impact of Scaling on Large Crossbar Arrays for Neuromorphic Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Large-scale crossbar arrays form the functional building block for neural networks that perform efficient inmemory computing with massive parallelism. In this paper, the impact of scaling of nano interconnects in large-sized crossbar arrays for neuromorphic applications is presented. Nanoscale interconnects are used to generate significantly larger crossbar arrays like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$64 \times 64,128 \times 128$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$256 \times 256$</tex> considering 13 nm and 7 nm technology nodes. These crossbar arrays are analyzed to study the effects of technology scaling and large arrays sizing on the key performance metrics like delay time, rise time and fall time.

articleTitle: A Multi-Output Active Learning Method for the Uncertainty Quantification of PCB Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel active learning method for iteratively building a suitable training set within the scope of Gaussian process models applied to the uncertainty quantification of multi-output system responses. In particular, the proposed strategy offers a significant advantage by extending the already existing generic techniques that typically account for a single scalar output only. This approach extends the training to all outputs, thus improving the accuracy of the overall response of the system in a more comprehensive manner.

articleTitle: SPICE-Based Behavioral Models of IC Buffers via Compact Kernel Regressions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This work presents a method for generating compact SPICE-compliant IC buffer models using the vector-valued Kernel Ridge Regression (VV-KRR). Power supply variations are captured, and model complexity is reduced with a compression technique based on the random sampling or the Nyström approximation. The compressed models are then implemented in SPICE, and their performance is evaluated on a realistic test case.

articleTitle: Tuning Unconventional Control Parameters for Optimal Transient Load Response in Multiphase Constant On-Time Switching Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Constant-on-time (COT) voltage regulation is a modern version of hysteretic control that has gained popularity for both single and multi-phase power converters [1]. Optimization of these converters gets progressively more challenging as the phase count and transient performance demands increase. This paper explores several unconventional controller design opportunities to enhance large current transient performance. We demonstrate how to optimize the non-linear frequency modulation combined with an AC loadline circuit to quell oscillatory behavior during large-signal loop closure. With the advent of trans-inductor voltage regulator (TLVR) coupled inductors the performance can be improved with less emphasis on the VR controller. Lastly, the error amplifier presents a significant bottleneck in the practical performance of the converter which is illustrated by simulation. The final 16-phase circuit performance is demonstrated with a 1000 A dynamic current excitation.

articleTitle: Voltage-Drop Analysis of 1R-1D Memristor Crossbar Arrays
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of memristor devices into 3D stacked arrays, focusing on the electrothermal interactions that affect the signal integrity. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10 \times 10 \times 1$</tex> crossbar array structure is analyzed, incorporating one-resistor-one-diode memristors. Two electrothermal models of the single memristor are proposed and cross-validated, one based on the finite-element-method numerical formulation of the multiphysics problem, the second based on a circuit equivalent representation. Both models are used to study the issue of the voltage drop across the array and its relation with the thermal responses, which can change the state of individual memristor cells and potentially lead to data loss. The role of the materials adopted to realize the array bars is also studied. In addition, the influence of the crossbar on the behavior of the single device is studied, by carrying out the analysis of the resistive switching behaviors, through the current-voltage characteristics.

articleTitle: Characterization of Miniaturized Transformers at Varying Operating Power
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: The trend towards miniaturization and integration, observed in all the fields of electronics, also applies to systems requiring galvanic isolation. A key aspect is the development of miniaturized transformers, to be integrated at silicon level or package level in a SoC (System-on-Chip) or SiP (System-in-Package) approach. This paper proposes a methodology to characterize such micro-transformers through electromagnetic simulations, extracting a set of key performance parameters, the accuracy of which was experimentally verified. Results are valid under certain load conditions and rated power level but, in a real application, devices need the flexibility to work in a certain range of operating power with a negligible performance variation. Focus of the work is to evaluate the effect of this variable power. The transformers geometry was initially optimized for a rated power of 1W. Different transformer configurations have been tested with power ranging from 0.6 W to 1.4 W, and checking the variation in terms of voltage ratio and efficiency. Depending on the application, this variation can be impactful or negligible. Additionally, results have been compared with similar transformers optimized for each specific power level, to verify the improvement in case of a dedicated optimization.

articleTitle: Power Integrity Performance Variation Induced by Degassing Holes in BGA Packages
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Degassing (or outgassing) is a standard procedure employed in laminate-based IC package design and manufacturing process. This technique consists of puncturing holes in large plane shapes of the package to allow gas bubbles (formed during the manufacturing process between the package layers) to escape. The risk of delamination is in this way reduced. Degassing holes are crucial in ensuring the device reliability, but their presence alters the design of the package, reducing the effective area dedicated to power and ground domains. This paper aims at understanding the impact of the degassing holes on key figures that determine the electrical performance of the IC-package power delivery network. Different examples are analyzed by electromagnetic simulations, to assess how the degassing effect changes as function of the impacted copper area. Results are discussed from package level and system level perspective. Some considerations on modeling techniques are finally presented, analyzing the trade-off between accuracy and complexity when degassing is taken into account by an electromagnetic solver.

articleTitle: Bayesian Optimization of Microwave Filters: a Physics-Informed Approach Using the Szegö Kernel
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This work presents a data-efficient approach for optimizing microwave devices by combining Bayesian optimization with physics-informed Gaussian process models. The proposed approach models complex-valued frequency responses as a function of design parameters and frequency instead of modeling an objective function, enabling dynamic optimization of devices with intricate performance criteria. The method is validated through the optimization of a zig-zag microstrip bandpass filter to achieve the desired transmission characteristics. This work highlights the potential of Bayesian optimization to reduce computational costs in microwave device design.

articleTitle: A Novel Termination Resistance-Controlled Passive Equalization Method for Signal Integrity Enhancement in High-Speed Channel
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel termination resistance-controlled passive equalization method for signal integrity (SI) enhancement in high-speed channel. The proposed approach combines a termination resistance control method with a passive equalizer (PEQ) to mitigate inter-symbol interference (ISI) and DC-level reduction. By boosting the receiver (RX) voltage, pre-emphasis and DC-level boosting are achieved, while the PEQ cancels ISI. To validate the proposed method, the eye diagram performance of a structure without a PEQ, the conventional PEQ, and the proposed method were compared in both non-return to zero (NRZ) and pulse amplitude modulation (PAM)-4 scenarios. The proposed method demonstrates better performance than the conventional PEQ and is more effective in PAM-4 scenarios.

articleTitle: Power-to-Control Crosstalk in Power Electronic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper deals with a signal integrity issue specific to power electronic circuits: the crosstalk noise between the power and control sections. The case study investigated here involves a test-bench board mounting a power electronic voltage regulator, where parasitic capacitances in the PCB layout cause the crosstalk noise. The problem is analyzed using simulation and experimental results. Additionally, the paper addresses the measurement challenges associated with the probes' impact.

articleTitle: Acyclic Connected Graph Optimization for Generative Measurement Based Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 29th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Measured S-parameters are extremely useful in characterizing a system, but are cumbersome to use in many contexts. When used in a simulation as a blackbox macromodel, artifacts from launch structures can obscure the details of the measured system and cannot be separated. This paper presents a genetic algorithm to automatically create surrogate models of measured S-parameters using an acyclic graph of transmission lines. The algorithm is further accelerated by smart evolution based on local fitness, and seeding of the initial generation based on simple deterministic heuristics. Surrogate models generated in this manner are easily used in simulators, enable what-if analysis, and identify impedance changes and stubs which help identify their sources and can be easily mapped to the underlying physical topology.
